paragraphs: When several reinforcement learning agents learn together, their updates combine noisy experience with information exchanged across a network. Understanding average convergence does not fully describe what happens during an individual run. This paper develops a law of the iterated logarithm for distributed nonlinear stochastic approximation, giving convergence rates along almost every sample path on which the algorithm converges.

That qualification matters: the result describes the speed of convergence on convergent paths. Its contribution goes beyond rates stated in expectation or through a central limit theorem. The analysis also relaxes two familiar requirements: the communication matrix need not be doubly stochastic, and the sum of squared step sizes need not be finite.

For distributed TD(0) with linear function approximation, the authors derive almost-sure rates of O(sqrt(n^(-gamma) log n)) for step sizes n^(-gamma), where 0 < gamma < 1. With step sizes of the 1/n type, the rate becomes O(sqrt(log log n / n)). These decay rates do not depend on the agents' interaction graph, sharpening the description of learning fluctuations across distributed runs.
neurips-2021-a-law-of-iterated-logarithm.tldr: The paper derives almost-sure convergence rates for distributed learning under weaker assumptions, including explicit rates for multi-agent TD(0).

paragraphs: A variational autoencoder learns a latent representation from which it can generate observations. When tasks arrive sequentially and only the current task's data remain available, learning new material can erase earlier capabilities. BooVAE addresses this continual learning problem by making the prior distribution over the latent space a central part of remembering tasks.

For each task, the method learns a prior that approximates the aggregated posterior, the collection of latent distributions produced when the encoder processes that task's observations. It represents this approximation as an additive mixture. Each component comes from evaluating the encoder on a trainable pseudo-input, giving the method adjustable building blocks for representing the task.

A greedy procedure resembling boosting adds components, while entropy regularization encourages their diversity. The goal is to remember each task with as few components as possible. The authors integrate this learned prior into an end-to-end continual learning system and evaluate it on MNIST, Fashion MNIST, NotMNIST, and CelebA. They report automatic avoidance of catastrophic forgetting on each tested dataset, supporting the prior's role as a practical memory mechanism.
neurips-2021-boovae-boosting-approach-fo.tldr: BooVAE learns compact mixture priors to preserve earlier tasks when a variational autoencoder learns from sequential datasets.

paragraphs: Statistical downscaling aims to recover a detailed spatial field using coarse measurements and finer-resolution information. A central difficulty is that observations from different datasets may not match directly. This paper considers a setting where coarse observations are conditional averages of fine observations, connected through a mediating variable observed throughout the domain.

Under that model, recovering the detailed field becomes an inverse problem: undoing a conditional expectation, which the authors call deconditioning. They formulate this problem in Bayesian terms using Gaussian processes. Conditional averages serve as inter-domain features of the underlying field, allowing the method to construct a posterior distribution for the fine-scale field rather than only a single reconstruction.

The framework recovers an earlier kernel formulation and adds an efficient conditional mean embedding estimator for data at multiple resolutions. The solution also admits an interpretation as a two-stage, vector-valued kernel ridge regression procedure. Under mild assumptions, the authors establish a minimax-optimal convergence rate. Synthetic and real atmospheric downscaling experiments show substantial improvements over existing methods, supporting the approach for the stated aggregation setting.
neurips-2021-deconditional-downscaling-w.tldr: A Bayesian deconditioning framework reconstructs fine spatial fields from conditional averages, with convergence guarantees and improved atmospheric downscaling results.

paragraphs: Many neural video compressors predict a frame and then encode the difference between that prediction and the actual frame. The paper argues that removing information shared across frames through simple subtraction leaves compression opportunities unused. It proposes conditional coding, in which learned context directly informs how the current frame is encoded and reconstructed.

The key design choice is to express that context in a feature space. These higher-dimensional features can carry rich information to both the encoder and decoder, giving the compression system more useful conditioning information. The authors connect this richer context to improved reconstruction of high-frequency image content, which matters for preserving fine visual detail.

The framework addresses how to define, use, and learn the conditioning information, while allowing its design to be changed within the same general approach. Experiments report substantial improvements over previous leading neural video compression methods. Against x265 with its veryslow preset, the method achieves a 26.0% bitrate saving on standard 1080P test videos. This result supports learned feature context as an effective way to exploit information shared across video frames.
neurips-2021-deep-contextual-video-compr.tldr: Learned feature context improves conditional video compression, delivering a reported 26.0% bitrate saving against x265 veryslow on standard 1080P videos.

paragraphs: Factor analysis makes large brain-imaging datasets easier to study by reducing them to smaller representations. However, many such methods overlook the nonlinear temporal behavior of neural processes. Deep Markov factor analysis addresses both parts of the problem together: the large number of spatial measurements and the complex way those measurements change over time.

The model represents temporal behavior through a chain of low-dimensional embeddings governed by a Markov structure. It combines this temporal representation with spatial inductive assumptions, using neural networks to relate the components. This generative formulation allows temporal dynamics and spatial structure to contribute jointly to the representation of functional magnetic resonance imaging data.

An additional discrete latent variable supports clustering within the temporal embedding, accounting for variation associated with subjects and cognitive states. Such groupings can help researchers examine neuroscientific hypotheses using fMRI observations. Experiments on synthetic and real fMRI data demonstrate interpretable clusters and the ability to capture nonlinear temporal dependencies. The stated findings support a representation that preserves useful temporal organization while reducing the spatial complexity of the measurements.
neurips-2021-deep-markov-factor-analysis.tldr: Deep Markov factor analysis jointly models spatial structure and nonlinear temporal dynamics to produce interpretable representations and clusters of fMRI data.

paragraphs: Distributed datasets can differ while still sharing useful structure. This paper studies a collection of sparse linear models connected by a graph: each node has its own dataset and model, and an edge indicates that neighboring models differ in only a small number of coordinates. The relationship is therefore expressed through sparse differences between solutions.

The proposed estimator combines Basis Pursuit Denoising with a total variation penalty. This couples model fitting across the graph, encouraging the differences between connected solutions to follow the assumed sparse structure. The authors establish finite-sample recovery guarantees for sub-Gaussian design matrices and analyze both noisy observations and the noiseless setting.

For a tree with a designated reference root, the analysis shows a sample advantage when differences across nodes are sparser than the root model itself. Under that condition, recovery needs fewer samples than independent fitting or approaches such as group Lasso that rely on substantial support overlap. Numerical work examines distributed ADMM methods and hyperspectral unmixing, connecting the recovery analysis to distributed computation and an application.
neurips-2021-distributed-machine-learnin.tldr: Coupling sparse local models through sparse graph differences can reduce sample requirements under the paper's stated recovery conditions.

paragraphs: Artificial agents can learn to communicate successfully while developing messages that people find difficult to interpret. The authors argue that a common training objective contributes to this problem: identifying one object in a shared visual scene can encourage overfitting to concrete references. It offers little pressure to develop messages expressing ideas that apply across objects.

The paper proposes communication games centered on generalizations over sets of objects representing abstract visual concepts. Agents must communicate something broader than the identity of a single item. The games can also give agents separate contexts, changing the information available to each participant while preserving the need to convey the relevant generalization.

Across several established metrics, these games substantially improve the systematicity and interpretability of the learned languages. The paper also introduces an analysis method that learns an approximate compositional reconstruction of a language to identify embedded logical operations. Together, the training and analysis contributions connect more abstract communication objectives with more structured emergent languages, while treating the reconstruction as approximate rather than a complete account of their meaning.
neurips-2021-emergent-communication-of-g.tldr: Training agents to communicate generalizations about object sets produces more systematic and interpretable languages in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Communicating gradients can limit the scalability of distributed training. Compressing them reduces communication, but it also changes the updates: convergence can slow, and biased compression can even cause divergence. A known remedy for stochastic gradient descent is to retain compression error and add it back during a later update.

This paper examines that remedy for a class of variance-reduced algorithms that smooth stochastic gradients through a moving average of gradient history. Its analysis shows that correcting with only the previous step's compression error does not fully compensate for the error in this setting. The proposed method instead uses errors from the previous two steps.

The authors show that this two-step correction can recover the same asymptotic convergence rate as training without compression. The result concerns the rate of convergence, giving theoretical support for reducing communication without losing that asymptotic behavior. They also provide a unified analysis framework covering the relevant variance-reduced algorithms both with and without error compensation. This clarifies why the correction must account for how historical gradients enter the update.
neurips-2021-errorcompensatedx-error-com.tldr: Using compression errors from two previous steps can restore uncompressed asymptotic convergence rates for the analyzed class of variance-reduced algorithms.

paragraphs: Connections between graph nodes provide useful information for predicting their classes. Those same connections also make predictions dependent, complicating the question of how uncertain each prediction should be. This paper focuses on uncertainty for node classification, where methods that exploit graph structure need an account of confidence as well as class predictions.

The authors first formulate three axioms describing expected uncertainty behavior in homophilic attributed graphs, where connected nodes tend to be similar and nodes carry features. They then introduce Graph Posterior Network, which explicitly performs Bayesian posterior updates for interdependent node predictions. The model is proved to satisfy the proposed axioms, linking its uncertainty behavior to stated formal requirements.

The empirical evaluation covers semi-supervised node classification, including the detection of anomalous features and classes omitted from training. GPN outperforms existing uncertainty estimation approaches in those experiments. The contribution combines a formal description of desirable behavior with a model designed to meet it and practical evaluation. Its theoretical claims remain tied to the proposed axioms and graph setting, while the experimental results address the tested uncertainty tasks.
neurips-2021-graph-posterior-network-bay.tldr: Graph Posterior Network uses Bayesian updates to estimate node uncertainty, satisfies proposed graph-specific axioms, and improves uncertainty estimation in experiments.

paragraphs: Adder neural networks replace costly multiplications with cheaper additions to reduce energy use. Their accuracy, however, can lag behind convolutional networks without additional training techniques. This paper investigates how the different similarity measurement between filters and features affects the geometry of learned features, focusing on distributions with heavy tails.

The authors identify unordered heavy tails as a possible key obstacle to classification performance: broader tails tend to overlap in feature space. They introduce predefined multivariate skew Laplace distributions into the loss function so that feature distributions can be shaped explicitly. This makes the arrangement of the tails a target of learning.

Their method handles existing heavy tails through a modification of the classifier. An angle-based constraint on distribution parameters encourages diverse tail directions as the features form clusters. The intended effect is to organize the tails that would otherwise overlap. Experiments across several benchmarks, including comparisons with alternative distributions, show improved AdderNet performance. The findings support distribution design as a useful approach to the observed accuracy gap without establishing heavy tails as its sole cause.
neurips-2021-handling-long-tailed-featur.tldr: Shaping heavy-tailed feature distributions through a modified classifier improves AdderNet performance in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Generating a sequence of images with gradual changes requires a way to control how appearance evolves. This paper places that control in the generator's convolutional filters. It decomposes high-dimensional filters into a set of smaller building blocks, called filter atoms, making a subspace of possible filters easier to model and sample.

The authors use a neural ordinary differential equation to model the filter atoms continuously. Adjusting the equation's integration interval changes their evolution and thereby controls changes in the generated images. They provide both theoretical and empirical support that the introduced continuity can propagate from the filter representation to the image output.

Experiments include image-to-image translation and generation conditioned on continuous labels. The framework enables gradual image manipulation without auxiliary network components or heavy supervision. Its central contribution is a way to navigate generated appearance through a structured subspace of network parameters. The reported results support filter atoms as an efficient control representation and show how continuous parameter evolution can become visible as gradual changes in generated content.
neurips-2021-image-generation-using-cont.tldr: Continuous filter atoms modeled by a neural differential equation let a generator produce controllable, gradual changes in image appearance.

paragraphs: Physical neurons take time to respond, so a hierarchy of neuronal layers can accumulate delays. These delays affect inference and can misalign network outputs with the signals used for learning. Latent Equilibrium addresses this timing problem by drawing on neurons' ability to advance their output relative to their membrane potential.

The framework uses that principle to enable quasi-instantaneous inference independent of network depth, without separate plasticity phases or expensive relaxation periods. The authors derive neuron and synapse dynamics together from a prospective energy function involving generalized position and momentum. The resulting dynamics can be interpreted as a biologically plausible approximation to backpropagation, with continuous-time leaky neurons and continuously active local plasticity.

Experiments demonstrate learning on standard benchmark datasets with competitive fully connected and convolutional models. The authors also apply the principle to detailed cortical microcircuit models and examine robustness to spatial and temporal imperfections in the underlying substrate. These investigations support feasibility for physical realization. The central claim concerns how the framework compensates for component delays, with quasi-instantaneous computation distinguished from a claim that physical neurons themselves respond instantaneously.
neurips-2021-latent-equilibrium-a-unifie.tldr: Latent Equilibrium uses prospective neuronal dynamics to compensate for slow components and support continuous local learning approximating backpropagation.

paragraphs: A learned Bayesian network must support reasoning as well as represent statistical relationships. This paper studies how to learn network structures that allow fast exact probabilistic inference. It focuses on the complexity measure used during learning, since a structural restriction is useful only insofar as it captures the work required for later inference.

The authors use maximum state space size in place of the more conventional treewidth measure. This is a finer-grained way to account for variables whose domains contain different numbers of possible values. Two structural choices can therefore have different reasoning costs because of their variable domains, a distinction the proposed measure explicitly accommodates.

The learning methods combine heuristic Bayesian network structure search with a MaxSAT-powered local improvement procedure. This connects a broad structure-learning process with targeted improvements guided by inference complexity. Experiments show that the resulting networks support significantly faster exact inference than networks learned under treewidth bounds. The stated result concerns inference speed and supports using a complexity measure that reflects domain sizes when constructing Bayesian networks for subsequent reasoning.
neurips-2021-learning-fast-inference-bay.tldr: Accounting for variable domain sizes during Bayesian network learning produces networks with faster exact inference than treewidth-bounded alternatives in experiments.

paragraphs: In many datasets, the causal relationships of interest concern hidden concepts rather than raw measurements. For an image, those concepts might be objects, while the observations are pixels. This paper studies recovery of the causal graph over latent variables while allowing the relationships involved to be general and potentially nonlinear.

The authors provide conditions under which both the latent representations and their causal model are identifiable. They establish this through a reduction to a mixture oracle. The central connection links determining the order of a mixture model with recovering the bipartite graph that connects observed variables to unobserved ones. This offers a route from mixture information to hidden graphical structure.

The proof is constructive, so the identifiability argument also leads to algorithms for explicitly reconstructing the full graphical model. The paper discusses efficient algorithms and includes experiments illustrating their use. Its contribution is therefore both a recovery result and an algorithmic pathway. The stated conditions are essential to interpreting the result: recovery of latent causal structure is established within that setting, rather than asserted for arbitrary observational data.
neurips-2021-learning-latent-causal-grap.tldr: Under stated identifiability conditions, mixture-oracle information enables constructive recovery of latent representations and their causal graph.

paragraphs: Iterative machine teaching selects examples based on a learner's current state, adapting instruction as learning proceeds. A computational bottleneck arises when the teacher scans the entire training set at every iteration to choose the next example. The paper targets this repeated search cost, which makes existing approaches difficult to use efficiently on Internet-of-Things devices.

Locality Sensitive Teaching replaces that expensive selection process with a framework based on locality sensitive sampling. The authors prove near-constant time complexity, an exponential improvement over the existing baseline's complexity. This changes the computational burden of selecting teaching examples, making the teaching procedure more suitable for devices with limited time and energy resources.

The reported evaluation reaches speedups of up to 425.12 times and energy savings of up to 99.76% relative to iterative machine teaching. These are maximum reported improvements, so they describe the strongest observed gains. The paper presents the framework as enabling efficient machine teaching on IoT devices, motivated by personalized education at home. Its main demonstrated benefit is the substantial reduction in the computational and energy costs of adaptive example selection.
neurips-2021-locality-sensitive-teaching.tldr: Locality Sensitive Teaching accelerates adaptive example selection with provable near-constant complexity and large reported time and energy savings.

paragraphs: Training data can influence a model through the order in which examples are presented as well as through their content. This paper studies attacks that alter only that order, leaving the underlying dataset and model architecture unchanged. It shows that control over training sequence can be enough to interfere with what a model learns.

The authors find that adversarial ordering can prevent learning or cause the model to acquire attacker-specified behaviors. In some cases, a single adversarially ordered epoch can slow learning or erase accumulated progress. The mechanism targets the stochastic nature of modern learning procedures, making the sequencing of otherwise unchanged examples a consequential part of training.

Evaluations on computer vision and natural language benchmarks demonstrate disruption of training and the introduction of backdoors. The findings establish an attack surface beyond changes to data content or architecture. The one-epoch result is a possibility demonstrated by the work, rather than a claim that every reordered epoch resets a model. Overall, the experiments show that preserving the dataset itself does not eliminate the training influence available through its presentation order.
neurips-2021-manipulating-sgd-with-data-.tldr: Adversarially ordering unchanged training examples can disrupt learning, erase progress, or introduce attacker-specified behaviors.

paragraphs: Complex activities involve several people and objects whose roles and relationships change over time. Recognizing the overall activity therefore requires more than assigning one label to a video. This paper defines activity parsing as locating and classifying activities, sub-activities, and atomic actions while also understanding individual actors, objects, and the relationships between them.

The authors argue that pairwise links do not adequately represent interactions involving multiple entities. They introduce an Action Hypergraph, a representation spanning space and time whose hyperedges express higher-order relationships. This gives the model a way to represent relationships involving several participants together, alongside the hierarchy of action parts that compose an activity.

The paper also introduces the Multi-Object Multi-Actor dataset and benchmark dedicated to activity parsing, along with the HyperGraph Activity Parsing network. HGAP outperforms several baselines, including methods using ordinary graphs and raw video data. These findings support the proposed representation for the tested task. The contribution combines a more detailed recognition objective, data for evaluating it, and a model that explicitly represents the multi-entity structure of complex activities.
neurips-2021-moma-multi-object-multi-act.tldr: MOMA introduces activity parsing, a dedicated benchmark, and a hypergraph model for understanding hierarchical actions involving multiple people and objects.

paragraphs: Diplomacy presents an enormous action space, with more than 10^20 possible actions per turn. This paper develops an algorithm for exploring combinatorial action spaces and approximating equilibria. It jointly performs value iteration and learns a policy proposal network, using a double-oracle step to discover additional actions worth including among the proposals.

At each state, an equilibrium search procedure supplies the target policy and state value used for training. With this approach, the authors train DORA from scratch for a popular two-player Diplomacy variant and demonstrate superhuman performance. They also extend the method to full-scale no-press Diplomacy, training an agent from scratch without human data.

The full-scale result raises a separate strategic issue. The authors present evidence that the learned strategy is incompatible with agents initialized from human data. They interpret this as strong evidence of multiple equilibria in Diplomacy and as suggesting that self-play alone may be insufficient for superhuman performance in the full game. The superhuman result belongs to the two-player variant; the broader game motivates a qualified conclusion about the limits of self-play.
neurips-2021-no-press-diplomacy-from-scr.tldr: DORA learns superhuman two-player Diplomacy from scratch, while full-scale experiments suggest strategic incompatibilities that may limit self-play alone.

paragraphs: Semantic segmentation usually assigns a class to every pixel, whereas instance segmentation often predicts masks and classifies them. This paper shows that mask classification is general enough to handle both tasks using the same model, loss, and training procedure. That observation provides a shared formulation for tasks commonly approached with different prediction designs.

The proposed model, MaskFormer, predicts a set of binary masks and assigns one global class prediction to each mask. Its basic output unit is therefore a labeled region. This formulation simplifies the range of approaches needed for semantic and panoptic segmentation, and the authors observe a particular advantage over per-pixel classification baselines when the class vocabulary is large.

The reported results surpass the semantic and panoptic state-of-the-art models used in the paper's comparisons. MaskFormer reaches 55.6 mIoU on ADE20K for semantic segmentation and 52.7 PQ on COCO for panoptic segmentation. These findings support mask classification as an effective unified approach. The central claim is that it is sufficiently general for both task types, with the empirical comparisons showing that this unification can also deliver strong performance.
neurips-2021-per-pixel-classification-is.tldr: MaskFormer unifies segmentation through labeled mask predictions and achieves strong semantic and panoptic results, especially relative to per-pixel baselines with many classes.

paragraphs: Mean-field reinforcement learning uses the interchangeability of homogeneous agents to handle large populations. Much prior work assumes that agents can interact with the environment during training. This paper addresses the offline setting, motivated by applications such as social welfare optimization where experimenting in the actual system can be prohibitive or ethically problematic.

The proposed SAFARI algorithm performs pessimistic mean-field value iteration using pre-collected experience. Its theoretical guarantee relies on a coverage assumption: the dataset must contain enough information about the optimal policy. This condition makes clear what the stored experience needs to support, even though training does not require new interaction with the environment.

For an episodic mean-field decision process with horizon H and N training trajectories, the authors bound the suboptimality gap by O(H^2 d_eff / sqrt(N)). Here d_eff measures the effective dimension of the value-function class. The bound is independent of the number of agents, which is the key scaling benefit for large homogeneous populations. Numerical experiments accompany the theory, while the guarantee links performance to data quantity, horizon, representation complexity, and the stated coverage condition.
neurips-2021-pessimism-meets-invariance-.tldr: SAFARI learns offline mean-field policies with a suboptimality guarantee independent of agent count, provided the dataset sufficiently covers the optimal policy.

paragraphs: Interactive learning lets an algorithm choose what information to request, as in active classification or identifying the best available arm. This paper studies the realizable setting, where the target is represented by the assumed function class. It begins by showing that agnostic algorithms cannot attain minimax-optimal performance in this setting, motivating methods that explicitly use realizability.

The authors develop two general-purpose greedy algorithms whose sample requirements match minimax lower bounds up to logarithmic factors. The framework accommodates function classes including kernel methods, Hölder-smooth functions, and convex functions. Its sample complexity can be expressed through established quantities such as extended teaching dimension and haystack dimension, connecting the algorithms to theoretical measures of interactive learning difficulty.

Computational efficiency comes from sampling candidate functions from the version space using Monte Carlo hit-and-run procedures, instead of explicitly maintaining that entire space. The methods can also incorporate prior knowledge. Experiments show performance competitive with Gaussian process UCB approaches. Together, the results connect near-optimal information use with a computationally efficient implementation, with the realizability assumption central to both the motivation and the guarantees.
neurips-2021-practical-provably-correct-.tldr: Two efficient interactive learning algorithms exploit realizability to achieve near-minimax sample complexity while supporting broad function classes and prior knowledge.

paragraphs: Machine unlearning asks how to modify a trained model when a training example must later be removed. This paper studies the problem through generalization: after unlearning, the model should still perform well on unseen samples from the original distribution. The initial dataset is assumed to contain independent, identically distributed samples from an unknown distribution.

The authors consider both the computation and storage required to support deletion requests. For convex losses, they provide an algorithm that can unlearn up to O(n / d^(1/4)) samples, where n is the training-set size and d is the problem dimension. This quantifies how the supported number of deletions scales with dataset size and dimensionality.

The comparison with differential privacy gives the result its broader significance. Differentially private learning implies unlearning, but in general it guarantees deletion of only O(n / d^(1/2)) samples. The different dimension dependence establishes a separation between the two approaches. Within the studied setting, directly designing for unlearning can support more deletions than the general differential-privacy guarantee, while retaining the paper's focus on accuracy for previously unseen data.
neurips-2021-remember-what-you-want-to-f.tldr: For convex losses, a dedicated unlearning algorithm supports more deletions in its dimension-dependent guarantee than general differentially private learning.

paragraphs: Diffusion models generate data by learning to reverse a corruption process. This paper develops discrete denoising diffusion probabilistic models, or D3PMs, for data with discrete states. The main extension is to allow structured transition probabilities during corruption, expanding beyond a process that treats transitions uniformly.

The authors investigate transition matrices that resemble Gaussian kernels, matrices based on neighboring items in an embedding space, and matrices containing absorbing states. The absorbing-state construction connects diffusion with autoregressive and mask-based generation. They also introduce a training objective combining a variational lower bound with an auxiliary cross-entropy loss. These choices make the corruption structure and learning objective explicit parts of model design.

Experiments show that the transition matrix affects performance in both image and text generation. The models achieve strong character-level text results and scale to large vocabularies on LM1B. On CIFAR-10, they approach the sample quality of a continuous-space DDPM while exceeding its log-likelihood. Those are distinct findings: visual sample quality is reported as approaching the comparison model, whereas likelihood is reported as better.
neurips-2021-structured-denoising-diffus.tldr: D3PMs use structured discrete corruption processes and a combined loss to improve diffusion-based image and text generation.

paragraphs: An active learner chooses an example and asks for its label. This paper adds a helpful teacher who supplies both that label and an additional contrastive example. The extra example must come from a set constrained by the learner's query, such as dissimilar instances sharing the same label. Its purpose is to guide learning more efficiently.

Choosing these examples creates a sequence optimization problem. A useful teaching decision depends on the preceding interactions, so selecting an informative example requires accounting for the learner's evolving situation. The authors investigate an efficient adaptive teaching algorithm that chooses contrastive examples as the interaction unfolds, aiming to accelerate the overall learning process.

They derive performance guarantees in terms of two problem-dependent parameters and obtain strong approximation guarantees for particular active learners, including generalized binary search. Two numerical case studies illustrate the bounds and demonstrate the framework's effectiveness. The work shows how explanatory examples can be treated as a structured teaching resource, with theoretical guarantees tied to the problem and learner rather than a universal claim that every additional example improves learning.
neurips-2021-teaching-an-active-learner-.tldr: An adaptive teacher can accelerate active learning by selecting query-constrained contrastive examples, with guarantees depending on the problem and learner.

paragraphs: Model selection for contextual bandits asks whether one learning algorithm can adapt to policy classes of different complexity. This paper considers nested classes and asks whether an algorithm can simultaneously achieve the optimal guarantees available for each class. It also examines a proposed tradeoff involving log(|Pi_m|)^(1-alpha) T^alpha, for alpha between one-half and one.

The authors show that these desired guarantees are unattainable for general policy classes, even when the environment is purely stochastic. They characterize the achievable compromises through a Pareto frontier, providing upper and lower bounds that match up to logarithmic factors. This identifies both attainable performance and barriers that no algorithm can avoid in the studied setting.

A central consequence is that an increase in the policy-class complexity term, independent of the time horizon T, is unavoidable. Adaptation therefore carries a cost beyond the proposed tradeoff. The negative result concerns general classes, preserving the scope of the impossibility claim. As an additional contribution, the paper resolves an open problem about second-order bounds in full-information games, extending its theoretical findings beyond contextual-bandit model selection.
neurips-2021-the-pareto-frontier-of-mode.tldr: Matching upper and lower bounds show unavoidable complexity costs when adapting across general nested policy classes in contextual bandits.
